segments: of Mush and its territory.
And he went to encamp against Khilat.
Balaban went out and seized the mountain passes against him,
and destroyed the majority of those who were with him.
And he, Najm al-Din, the son of al-Adil, escaped with a few wounded men to Mayperqat. And in the same year, the Iberians took the city of Kars, which belonged to the domain of Khilat,
after many years during which they had besieged it with battles and confinement, and had cut off supplies from it.
And in the year 1515 [of the Greeks],
[that is,] 604 of the Arabs [1207-1208 AD]:
al-Malik al-Awhad sent to his father al-Malik al-Adil,
and requested assistance in order to take Khilat.
And al-Malik al-Ashraf was sent to him with a large force,
and they came near to Khilat.
And Balaban went out and engaged them,
and he was unable to hold out,
but fled from before them and entered Khilat.
And he sent an envoy to Mughith al-Din [son of] Qilij Arslan, the lord of Erzurum,
and called him to his aid.
And he came in person,
and Balaban went out to meet him.
And they both encountered al-Malik al-Awhad and his brother,
and they routed them and put them to flight.
And they went and encamped against Mush,
and they were close to taking it.
Then the son of Qilij Arslan acted treacherously against Balaban and killed him,
so that he himself might rule over Khilat.
And when he went against Khilat,
the people of Khilat shut the gates in his face.
And he went from there to Manazgird (Malazgird),
and those who were in it did likewise.
And when hope was cut off,
he left and went to his own country.
And the people of Khilat sent to al-Malik al-Awhad and brought him,
and they surrendered Khilat to him.
Now, the Arab rulers who were in the surrounding region,
because it did not please them that the son of al-Adil should rule,
since they feared his father,
were constantly sending [raiders] and pillaging the territory of Khilat, and especially the Iberians.
And also some of the amirs of Khilat rebelled against al-Awhad,
and seized the fortress of Van,
than which there is none stronger in that region,
and they also gained control over Arjish.
And after many hardships, al-Awhad was able to take Van from them,
when he sent and brought his brother al-Ashraf.
And the people of Khilat regretted that they had surrendered Khilat to the house of al-Adil.
